title: The Plaster Moth's Crumbling Aqueduct
story: Tasselvex the Plaster Moth has been nibbling the mortar out of the great desert aqueduct, and the village of Dry Hollow is down to its last cupful of water. Mr 6 climbs the sun-baked arches with a mixing trough and the old mason's recipe: patch-mortar must be mixed 3 parts resin to 5 parts river-silt to 2 parts ash. He needs 60 buckets of mortar to seal every nibbled crack.
question: Mr 6 already has 12 buckets of river-silt in his cart. How many more buckets of river-silt must he gather to mix the full 60 buckets of mortar?
solution: Add the recipe parts: 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 equal parts, so each part is 60 ÷ 10 = 6 buckets.
He already has 12, so 30 - 12 = 18 more buckets of river-silt.
praise: Breaking the recipe into equal parts was smart thinking — the missing move was subtracting the 12 buckets already in the cart.
hint: First add 3 + 5 + 2 to see how many equal shares the 60 buckets split into.
victory: The patched aqueduct gurgles back to life, and Tasselvex — discovering that dried patch-mortar tastes like chalky regret — flutters off to nibble sand dunes instead.
imagePrompt: A small numeral-six knight with a trowel standing on a towering sandstone aqueduct arch, a dusty pale moth the size of a horse flaking mortar from the stones, golden desert light and a thin bright ribbon of water returning below.
